items.title: Trezor Says a Shipping Partner Exposed Customer Data
points: A third-party shipping partner contracted by Trezor exposed customer personal data, according to company disclosures.
The breach occurred at the fulfillment stage (order shipping/logistics) rather than within Trezor's core systems, so the hardware wallet's cryptographic security was not directly compromised.
The incident highlights supply chain risks in hardware wallet distribution, where customer addresses and order info are handled by external logistics providers.
Users' actual crypto assets stored on their devices remain protected, as the breach did not affect private key management or on-device security mechanisms.

items.title: CFTC Approves Blockchain-Based Derivatives Infrastructure
points: The CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the US derivatives regulator) approved Backpack and tZERO to operate blockchain-based regulated derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses.
This marks the first regulated pathway for onchain (recorded directly on a blockchain) trading infrastructure in the US.

items.title: MEGA's $30M Pivot to Inference Markets
points: MegaETH rebranded as MEGA and committed $30M from its treasury to launch an AI inference market in December, after acknowledging it failed to achieve product-market fit (clear evidence users want what's being built).
Total value locked (TVL, total crypto assets deposited in a protocol) collapsed from $245M in May 2026 to under $10M, prompting the pivot.

The inference market targets a 'supply paradox' where buyers overpay for identical open-source AI models from familiar providers; MEGA's 'Purified Intelligence' verification layer concept cites three possible solutions (fingerprinting, TEE-sealed hardware, cryptographic proofs) without committing to one.

Clearest differentiation comes from prompt privacy (hiding user queries) and forward capacity markets letting buyers reserve and trade specific model/volume/performance windows, pricing future model output rather than raw GPU hours.

items.title: Toss Launches Non-Custodial Crypto Wallet in South Korea
points: South Korean fintech Toss is launching a non-custodial (user holds their own private keys, not the company) crypto wallet within its app.
It will support ETH, USDT, and USDC for over 30 million users, about 60% of South Korea's population.

items.title: Standard Chartered: Japanese Bond Tokenization Could Drive RWA Boom
points: Tokenizing Japanese government bonds could help grow the real-world asset (RWA, physical assets converted into blockchain tokens) market from $45B to $2T by end-2028, per Standard Chartered.

items.title: Solana Launches Confidential Compute
points: Solana Foundation launched Confidential Compute, using TEE (trusted execution environment, secure hardware that hides data even from the host machine) technology.
The feature enables private AI inference and confidential smart contracts (programmable blockchain agreements) on Solana.

items.title: Wintermute's $10M Annual Latency Arbitrage on Hyperliquid
points: Wintermute spends roughly $10M per year (~$26,000/day) to control 76% of Hyperliquid's gossip priority auction slots, gaining a 50-60ms latency edge in a system that re-auctions queue priority every three minutes.
The speed edge lets Wintermute cancel orders before large trades land, adjust quotes toward incoming flow, and cross-venue hedge on Binance before Hyperliquid reprices.
This has generated $227M in lifetime platform profits and $18.8M in the past 30 days for the firm.

Full access requires a direct Foundation node connection gated at ~0.5% of network maker volume plus 10,000 HYPE staked (~$18.9M), locking out smaller market makers and widening altcoin spreads at retail traders' expense.

items.title: Crypto Industry Wealth Decline Outpaces Revenue Growth
points: ETH and SOL price declines since October 2024 erased about $350B in industry wealth while revenue grew only about $8B, explaining sector gloom despite bullish macro signals.
With $26.6B in annual cash inflows, closing the $350B gap via revenue alone would require 35x growth, equivalent to 350 Hyperliquid-scale businesses.

Potential recovery paths include revenue-generating tokens like HYPE scaling up, or native asset appreciation requiring over 60% BTC price movement (adjusted for ETF holders who don't recycle capital), with 2027/2028 seen as the likely recovery window.

items.title: User-Generated Prediction Markets Finally Scale via XO Market
points: Most prediction market volume is concentrated in a few markets: 70% of Polymarket's closed markets cleared under $10K, and only 35% of Kalshi's 7.6M combo tickers saw any activity; no major venue allowed user-created markets until XO Market launched.
Augur's 2018 attempt showed demand but failed due to cheap abuse bonds, exploitable vague resolution rules, low-cost wash trading, and a slow 60-day dispute fork process.
XO Market addresses these issues with a $10 mandatory seed order, AI-based rule pre-screening, liquidity rewards tied to real trading, and 20% fee rebates to market creators.
XO Market reports $783M in cumulative notional volume across more than 3,000 user-created markets, 12 months after its November 2025 mainnet launch.
